<section id="about" class="academic-section about-section">
  <h2>About Me</h2>
  <p class="about-lead">
    I am a Ph.D. Candidate in Naval Architecture and Ocean Engineering at
    Universidad Polit&eacute;cnica de Madrid (UPM), Spain.
  </p>
  <p>
    I was born in 1999 in a small town in Anhui Province, China. I received my
    bachelor’s and master’s degrees from Wuhan University of Technology (WHUT)
    in 2020 and 2023, respectively. Since September 2023, I have been pursuing
    a PhD at the Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM), supported by an FPI
    fellowship from the Spanish Government.
  </p>
  <p>
    Before beginning my PhD, my research focused on ship–bridge collisions,
    risk and reliability analysis, and protective fender design. I continue to
    collaborate with colleagues in these areas, particularly on transferring
    collision-safety knowledge to offshore structures. I graduated with
    distinction from WHUT at both the undergraduate and master’s levels. During
    my studies, I received several scholarships and honours for academic
    achievement, student leadership, and community engagement. My master’s
    thesis was also recognised as an Outstanding Thesis in Hydraulic
    Engineering among China’s higher education institutions.
  </p>
  <p>
    My doctoral research focuses on the hydrodynamics of heave plates for
    floating offshore platforms. I combine physical experiments with
    high-fidelity CFD simulations, using experimental measurements to calibrate
    and validate numerical models. Through this work, I developed an
    OpenFOAM-based forced-oscillation testing framework that achieved accuracy
    among the highest reported to date. I have investigated the hydrodynamic
    performance of single, double, and perforated heave plates, providing
    practical guidance for engineering applications. Building on my background
    in structural mechanics, I have also conducted full-scale fluid–structure
    interaction analyses to examine failure modes and optimise stiffener
    configurations.
  </p>
  <p>
    As my doctoral research enters its final stage, my interests are expanding
    towards floating platforms for offshore renewable energy. Current topics
    include floating photovoltaic systems, the co-location of different
    renewable-energy technologies, shared mooring systems, and offshore
    structural safety. I welcome opportunities to exchange ideas and develop
    collaborations in these areas.
    <strong>I am also interested in suitable postdoctoral opportunities and
    expect to defend my PhD thesis around July 2027.</strong>
  </p>
  <p>
    Outside academia, I am an amateur photographer with a passion for natural
    landscapes. Badminton is my favourite sport, and I also enjoy watching
    football, especially when Spain is playing. ¡Vamos, España!
  </p>

  <div class="interest-row" aria-label="Research interests">
    <span>Floating Marine Structures</span>
    <span>Offshore Renewable Energy</span>
    <span>Hydrodynamics</span>
    <span>Collision and Safety</span>
  </div>
</section>
